title: Kirby Problem 2.22
statement:
Does every Lefschetz fibration over the 2–sphere admit a sec-
tion?
background:
Source: Kirby's Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology notes. Original problem number: KP-2.22.

Literature notes:
(1) Here we assume the fibration has critical points; otherwise, there exist
$T^{2}$–bundles over $S^{2}$ without sections.
Lefschetz fibrations that arise from blowing up the base locus of Lef-
schetz pencils naturally admit sections—namely, the exceptional divisors.
However, if say the fibration is constructed through branched covers, or ab-
stractly via a group-theoretic factorization, it is not a priori clear whether
a section exists.

Equivalently, one can ask if every positive Dehn twist factorization of
the identity in $\operatorname{Mod}(S_{g})$ lifts to $\operatorname{Mod}(S_{g}, p)$, the mapping class group of
the (fiber) surface fixing a point $p \in \Sigma_{g}$.
(2) This question has been raised repeatedly in the literature; e.g. [Smi01a,
Aur05, Ona10, Gom25], and Problems 2.8, 4.1, 7.1 and 8.1 in [Kor06],
[Sti15], [KS09], and [End21] respectively.
(3) More generally we can ask about the existence of multisections (in the
sense of [DS03, BH16b]):
Question. Does every Lefschetz fibration over the 2–sphere admit a
multisection? How about a 2-section?
Similarly, one can reformulate the existence of an $n$–section in terms of
the existence of a lift of a positive Dehn twist factorization of the identity
in $\operatorname{Mod}(S_{g})$ to a positive factorization also involving positive arc twists in
$\operatorname{Mod}(S_{g}, \{p_{1},..., p_{n}\})$, the mapping class group of $S_{g}$ fixing the set of $n$
distinct points $p_{1},..., p_{n} \in S_{g}$ [BH16b, BH16a].
(4) It is worth noting that for achiral Lefschetz fibrations, where the Dehn
twists in the factorization can be a mix of right-handed and left-handed
twists, there are counterexamples to the question. For instance, there is a
genus–1 achiral Lefschetz fibration on $S^{4}$ [Mat82], which, for homological
reasons, cannot admit a section. (In contrast, every genus–1 Lefschetz
fibration admits a section.) More examples are given in a recent preprint
of Gompf [Gom25].
(5) An ad hoc method for finding sections of a Lefschetz fibration with an
explicit monodromy factorization is to reverse-engineer the monodromy
factorization using elementary relations (among Dehn twists) in the map-
ping class group (e.g., [KO08, Ham17, Tan12]).
A potential counterexample to the existence of a section, where this ad
hoc method essentially fails, is the (spin, signature-zero) genus–9 Lefschetz
fibration of Baykur–Hamada in [BH24c].

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-17)

**Status:** open  
**Classification:** OPEN-TRIAGE

**Current literature assessment.** No theorem that every nontrivial Lefschetz fibration over S2 has a section or multisection was verified.

**Verified partial progress.**

- Lefschetz pencils yield examples with sections after blow-up.
- The question has equivalent mapping-class lifting formulations.

**Full solution or refutation.**

The general section and multisection questions remain open.

**What remains.**

Prove existence or construct a fibration without the proposed section/multisection.

**Sources checked.**

- K3: A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology, Problem 2.22 (2026). (authoritative_secondary): https://aimath.org/pastworkshops/kirbylistrep.pdf
  Evidence used: Maintained list poses the section/multisection questions.

**Review notes.** No source alteration.
